selection.summary: Issue #1241: the first input position can be invalid for a match on first usage of a context, because the match finder reference index starts at 0. The fix is to start the reference at 1 so that index 0 is never treated as a valid match position. Relevant evidence: ZSTD_window_update() in zstd_compress_internal.h (h0/h5, lines ~649-691) computes distanceFromBase = nextSrc - base and sets base = ip - distanceFromBase on non-contiguous segments; with a fresh/zeroed window this makes the first position index 0, which hash-chain/dfast tables treat as a valid (offset-0) match candidate. The window struct definition and initialization/reset path (h6/h7/h8, ZSTD_window_init/ZSTD_window_clear and ZSTD_window_t fields base/dictBase/lowLimit/dictLimit/nextSrc, plus validity check index >= lowLimit) show where the reference must be offset by 1. Match-finder first-use sites are in zstd_ldm.c (h3) and the block compression entry points in zstd_compress.c (h2) and zstdmt_compress.c (h4), which call ZSTD_window_update on the first block of a new context. Applying the fix: initialize/advance the base reference so the first input position maps to index 1 (e.g., in the reset/init path set nextSrc/base such that distanceFromBase accounts for the +1 offset, keeping the index >= lowLimit validity check correct), avoiding the problematic 0 index during first context usage.
